questions.question: Which Five-year Plan focused on infrastructure development, that is, power and transport?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** **____**First.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The correct answer is option 1, which is the First Five-Year Plan. This plan was launched in 1951 with the aim of boosting the Indian economy after independence.**
 
• **The First Five-Year** Plan focused on infrastructure development, including power and transport, which were essential for economic growth. 
 
• The plan aimed to increase the availability of electricity and improve transport networks such as roads, railways, and ports.
 
• The plan also focused on agricultural development, which was the backbone of the Indian economy at that time. 
 
• The government aimed to increase agricultural production and improve irrigation facilities.
 
• **The First Five-Year Plan was based on the Soviet model of planned developmen**t, which emphasized state control over the economy.
 
• The plan was successful in achieving its objectives and laid the foundation for future economic growth in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961) **focused on industrialization and **emphasized the development of heavy industries such as steel and machinery.**
 
• **The Third Five-Year Plan (1961-1966) **aimed to achieve self-sufficiency in** food production and increase agricultural productivity.**
 
• **The Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974)** focused on the removal of **poverty and the development of rural areas.**
 
• **The Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-1978)** aimed to achieve rapid economic growth and focused on the** development of small-scale industries and the expansion of the public sector.**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of metamorphic rocks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Granite.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Granite is an example of an igneous rock, not a metamorphic rock.**
 
• **Metamorphic rocks **are formed by transforming existing rocks** under heat and pressure.**
 
• **Quartzite** is a metamorphic rock formed from** sandstone.**
 
• **Gneiss** is a metamorphic rock formed from** shale or granite.**
 
• **Schist** is a metamorphic rock formed from **shale, slate, or phyllite.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quartzite** is a hard, durable rock often used for **building and decorative purposes.**
 
• **Gneiss is a foliated rock **with distinct banding patterns commonly used as a building material.
 
• **Schist is a foliated rock **with a characteristic layered appearance used for decorative purposes.

questions.question: Which of the following is not one of the five basic food groups suggested by the Indian Council of Medical Research?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is**__ __**__**Carbohydrates and Proteins.**__

__
 
• **Indian Council of Medical Research suggests five basic food groups for a healthy diet.**
 
• **Carbohydrates and Proteins are not **included in the list of** basic food groups suggested by the Indian Council of Medical Research.**
 
• Carbohydrates and Proteins are macronutrients that are essential for a** healthy diet, but they are not considered as a separate food group.**
 
• Consuming a balanced diet that includes all the necessary nutrients in the right proportion is important to maintain good health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Milk and meat products are rich sources of protein, calcium, and other essential nutrients.
 
• Pulses and legumes are good protein, fiber, and other essential nutrient sources.
 
• Fruits and vegetables are rich sources of vitamins, minerals, and fiber.
 
• Cereals and grains are good sources of carbohydrates, fiber, and other essential nutrients.

questions.question: The Governor of State possesses the pardoning power under which Article of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** **____**Article 161.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The answer to the given question is option 2, i.e., Article 161.**
 
• The pardoning power is the power to grant a reprieve or pardon to a person convicted of a crime.
 
• This power is vested in the Governor of a State under **Article 161 of the Constitution of India.**
 
• The Governor can **grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment or suspend, remit, or commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offense against any law relating to a matter to which the executive power of the State extends.**
 
• However, the Governor cannot pardon a** person who has been sentenced to death without consulting with the Council of Ministers of the State.**
 
• The pardoning power of the Governor is an important constitutional check on the judiciary and ensures that justice is tempered with mercy.
 
• Hence, the statement is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Article 163** of the Constitution deals with the **Council of Ministers, which aids and advises the Governor of a State.**
 
• **Article 55 **pertains to the election of the **President of India.**
 
• ** Article 145 **specifies the rules and procedures to be followed by the** Supreme Court of India.**

options.text: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

questions.solution:

__

• **NITI Aayog**, or the National Institution for Transforming India, was established on January 1, 2015, as a policy think tank and advisory body to the Government of India.

• It is constituted every five years and consists of a chairman and other members appointed by the President of India. 
 
 
 
• **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)**:
 
 
• SEBI is the regulatory body for the securities market in India.
 
• It was established in 1992 and operates under the **Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992. **

questions.question: Which among the following is the oldest vedas?

• It is divided into two main sections: **the "Black Yajurveda" (Krishna Yajurveda) and the "White Yajurveda" (Shukla Yajurveda).**
 
• The Yajurveda provides instructions and mantras for** performing rituals, including sacrificial offerings.**

questions.question: In economics, CRR stands for ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cash Reserve Ratio**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In economics, **CRR stands for Cash Reserve Ratio**.
 
• This term is often used in the** context of banking, particularly in India**.
 
• **The Cash Reserve Ratio** is a certain percentage of **bank deposits **that banks are required to keep with the **central bank (like the Reserve Bank of India, if we're discussing the Indian context).**
 
• This ratio is one of the instruments in the** toolkit of the central bank **used to** control liquidity in the banking system.**
 
• **A higher CRR** means that banks have less money available to lend out, which can help to slow down the **economy if it is overheating**.
 
• Conversely,** a lower CRR can stimulate economic activity by allowing banks to lend more money**.
 
• The central bank changes the** CRR** as per the requirements of the** economy**.
